properties.name: The unmodelled-source note is scoped to what this change touched, and says so when git cannot tell it
properties.rationale:
REFINES OPTION (a) OF `dec:idea-what-watches-for-the-last-responsible-moment-to-arrive`; IT DOES NOT SETTLE IT. That option — the gate sweeps the roots the design points at and notes files no Artifact claims — had already landed as a whole-tree note. Measured 2026-08-23: on this repo it reports 107 files, and a dev_storyflow agent independently named that aggregate framing as one of seven reasons it stopped reaching for reflow2 at all ("391 is not a number anybody can act on ... three gaps on the node I just edited would have been a task"). The session that read that report had skimmed the same 107-file note earlier the same day. So the finding now LEADS with the subset this working copy touched — usually two or three files — and the whole-tree count still prints beneath it.

OPTIONS (b), (c) AND (d) ARE UNTOUCHED and the decision stays `proposed`. What watches for the last responsible moment is still Anthony's to answer; this only makes one of the four less skimmable.

IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONFLATE NOTICING WITH DEMANDING — the counter-argument recorded beside that decision, and the reason severity is unchanged. The note says registering is an OFFER, and `dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment` is cited in the text a reader sees.

HONEST ABSENCE IS PART OF THE FEATURE: `_changed_paths` returns None rather than an empty set when git cannot answer, and the gate then says the measurement was NOT COMPUTED. A detector with nothing to run on must not read like one that ran clean.

⚠️ VOCABULARY NOTE, filed because it is the THIRD instance of one class. This event is joined to that Decision through GOVERNED_BY on a `*` wildcard, because NO EDGE TYPE NAMES BOTH ChangeEvent AND Decision. dev_storyflow reported the same shape twice in the days before — no edge for "this file is the executable form of that check" (Artifact→Verification), and SUPERSEDES refused between two Verifications. The pattern they name holds here: relationships between RECORDS are thinner in the vocabulary than relationships to Requirements.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: The unmodelled-source finding leads with the files this change touched; the whole-tree count still follows it. Severity unchanged — still a note, still an offer. Says so explicitly when git cannot tell it what changed.
